![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/2bb25857047d7a0200d4c58ee3756b0efa0f2d13aaca8664b1fe49414c18a461.png)

Consider the set $A,$ shown above. The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072304/assets/88f35519cf1aa01bcc9e4fb91b24c2bc2a1a823867ec2670563b0b45f2643a0a.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the parabola ${y}^{2}=-x.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{y}^{2}=-x\,}.
$$
